labels.rates: ESTIMATE (FWER, power and calls: binomial rates with Wilson 95% intervals)

why: bench/results/cpu-ladder.json: lab_today (7.52 s/study) is features + 1,000-permutation inference, its ladder rows are feature-only, so it marks matched_full_pipeline_speedup UNMEASURED. Here both arms do features and the per-study decision on the same studies.

scope.lab: cKDTree re-imaging + stats.permutation_test (1,000 within-strata shuffles), call p <= 0.05; 8 single-thread pool workers, one study each at a time (equal hardware); fixed sample of the first 200 null and 200 alternative studies
scope.preflight: Numba CSR re-imaging + Cox score screen, call maxT > design threshold from the 1000 calibration nulls; 8 single-thread workers; calibration counted
scope.both: same container, design bench.real_cpu.DESIGN, same seeds (SeedSequence([20261121, stream, i])), outcomes atlas.simulation (SYNTHETIC). Walls are compute through scoring: re-imaging and the per-study test or screen. The timer stops before the threshold, the calls and data load, and excludes outcome simulation, adjacency and JIT warm-up; wall.with_setup adds the setup back (not data load, threshold or calls). The lab ran a sample, so compare per-study wall only

headline: Per study, compute through scoring: lab 0.964 s on 8 cores (400 studies) vs Preflight 0.1737 s on 8 cores (2000 decided studies, 1000 calibration nulls paid for): 5.6x compute through scoring; 3.8x including outcome simulation, adjacency and warm-up. Features bitwise on 400 shared studies: True; decisions agree 362/400.

summary.rule: per-study conditional maxT, 1000 within-strata shuffles, p <= 0.05

projection.assumes: each design point costs what the measured point (bench.real_cpu.DESIGN) costs per study; real points differ in regions, field of view and mis-call rate. A projection, not a run.
